stem: Congenital rubella syndrome includes deafness together with which other features?

options.label: A
options.text: Neural tube defects and cleft palate
options.misconception: Assumes every teratogen produces the same pattern of birth defects.
options.explanation: Neural tube defects and cleft palate are linked to folate deficiency and teratogens such as valproate, not to congenital rubella.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Confuses congenital rubella with the late stigmata of congenital syphilis.
options.explanation: Saddle nose and notched (Hutchinson) incisors are stigmata of congenital syphilis, not of congenital rubella syndrome.

options.label: C
options.text: Limb hypoplasia and cicatricial skin scars
options.misconception: Confuses congenital rubella with congenital varicella syndrome.
options.explanation: Limb hypoplasia and cicatricial skin scarring are the hallmarks of congenital varicella syndrome after maternal chickenpox.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Mistakes features of congenital hypothyroidism for those of a congenital infection.
options.explanation: Macroglossia and umbilical hernia suggest congenital hypothyroidism, a non-infectious cause of neonatal findings.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None — CRS combines deafness, eye defects such as cataracts, and heart defects.
options.explanation: CDC lists deafness, eye abnormalities (cataracts, glaucoma, retinopathy, microphthalmia) and congenital heart disease among CRS birth defects.

context: Learning objective: Congenital rubella syndrome includes deafness, eye abnormalities (cataracts, glaucoma, retinopathy, microphthalmia) and congenital heart disease.
